observation_summary: The containsIgnoreCase method fails to correctly identify matches or non-matches when running in specific locales, leading to assertion failures in tests.
reasoning_summary: The original implementation of StringUtils.containsIgnoreCase used String.toUpperCase() to perform case-insensitive comparisons. Because String.toUpperCase() is locale-sensitive, it produces different results depending on the default locale of the JVM (e.g., the Turkish locale treats 'i' differently). This causes the method to behave inconsistently across different environments. The fix replaces the locale-dependent conversion with String.regionMatches(true, ...), which performs a locale-independent, case-insensitive comparison, ensuring consistent behavior regardless of the system locale.
